source_text: Et quid non habent, ait mihi aliquis, qui haec habent? tu dicis: habent baptismum Christi? dico. tu dicis: habent fidem Christi? dico. si ergo haec habent, quid non habent? quid est baptismus? sacramentum. audi apostolum: si sciero omnia sacramenta. multum est scire omnia dei sacramenta; quantacumque sciamus sacramenta, quis nouit dei omnia sacramenta? quid ait apostolus? si sciero omnia sacramenta, si habeam omnem prophetiam, adde adhuc: et omnem scientiam. (sed de fide dixeras). audi adhuc: si habeam omnem fidem. difficile est habere omnem fidem, quomodo difficile est noscere omnia sacramenta. et quid est quod dicit: (omnem) ita ut montes transferam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil sum? intendite, fratres, intendite, obsecro uos, apostoli uocem et uidete, quare cum tantis laboribus et periculis fratres nostros quaeramus. caritas eos quaerit de cordibus nostris. propter fratres meos et propinquos meos, dicit psalmus, loquebar pacem de te, ad sanctam Hierusalem loquens. uidete ergo, fratres mei, quid dixit apostolus: si habuero omnia sacramenta, omnem scientiam, prophetiam, fidem — qualem fidem? — ita ut montes transferam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil sum. non dixit: illa omnia nihil sunt,\' sed: si caritatem non habeam, nihil sum. quis enim demens diceret: nihil sunt dei sacramenta? quis demens diceret: nihil est prophetia, nihil scientia, nihil fides? non illa nihil sunt, sed cum illa magna sint, ego magna habens si caritatem non habeam, nihil sum. magna illa sunt et magna habeo et nihil sum, si caritatem non habeo, per quam mihi prosunt quae magna sunt. si enim non habeo caritatem, illa inesse possunt, prodesse non possunt.
thought_title: The gifts are great, but without love the person is nothing
orientation: Augustine is answering an imagined objector who asks what the Donatists lack, since they have Christ's baptism and faith.
pass_a_gloss: And what not [do] they have, says to me someone, who these things have? you say: [do] they have [the] baptism of Christ? I say. you say: [do] they have [the] faith of Christ? I say. if therefore these things they have, what not [do] they have? what is [the] baptism? [a] sacrament. hear [the] apostle: if I shall know all [the] sacraments. [it is] much to know all [the] sacraments of God; however many we know [the] sacraments, who knows [the] all [the] sacraments of God? what says [the] apostle? if I shall know all [the] sacraments, if I shall have all prophecy, add still: and all knowledge. (but about faith you had spoken). hear still: if I shall have all faith. [it is] difficult to have all faith, just as [it is] difficult to know all [the] sacraments. and what is [it] that he says: (all) so that [the] mountains I may move, [the] love however not I may have, nothing I am? pay attention, brothers, pay attention, I beseech you, [to the] voice of [the] apostle and see, why with so great labors and dangers [our] brothers our we seek. love them seeks from [the] hearts our. for [the sake of] [the] brothers my and [the] neighbors my, says [the] psalm, I was speaking peace about you, to [the] holy Jerusalem speaking. see therefore, [the] brothers my, what said [the] apostle: if I shall have all [the] sacraments, all knowledge, prophecy, faith — what kind of faith? — so that [the] mountains I may move, [the] love however not I may have, nothing I am. not he said: those all nothing are, but: if [the] love not I may have, nothing I am. who for [is] mad [who] would say: nothing are [the] sacraments of God? who [is] mad [who] would say: nothing is prophecy, nothing knowledge, nothing faith? not those nothing are, but when those great are, I [the] great things having if [the] love not I may have, nothing I am. great those are and great things I have and nothing I am, if [the] love not I have, through which to me profit which great are. if for not I have [the] love, those to be in [me] can, to profit not can.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'love' for caritas, not 'charity,' to keep the sense of the love that makes all gifts profitable.
The plural 'sacramenta' is rendered as 'sacraments' to preserve the general sense of sacred signs, not just baptism.
The literal 'I am nothing' keeps the apostle's stark contrast between possessing great gifts and being nothing without love.
'We seek' preserves the present deliberative force of the subjunctive, showing the ongoing effort to find the brothers.
The psalm quote uses 'propinquos' for those near, and 'neighbors' is the standard English for this relational term.
The literal 'they cannot benefit' with the implied object 'me' keeps the personal force of the apostle's argument.

pass_b_english: And what do they lack, someone says to me, who have these things? You say they have the baptism of Christ? I do. You say they have the faith of Christ? I do. So if they have these things, what do they lack? What is baptism? A sacrament. Listen to the apostle: If I know all sacraments. It is a great thing to know all the sacraments of God; however many sacraments we may know, who knows all the sacraments of God? What does the apostle say? If I know all sacraments, if I have all prophecy, add still more: and all knowledge. But you had spoken about faith. Listen further: if I have all faith. It is difficult to have all faith, just as it is difficult to know all sacraments. And what is it that he says: all faith, so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing? Pay attention, brothers, pay attention, I beg you, to the apostle's voice, and see why we seek our brothers with such labors and dangers. Love seeks them from our hearts. For the sake of my brothers and my neighbors, the psalm says, I was speaking peace about you, speaking to holy Jerusalem. See then, my brothers, what the apostle said: If I have all sacraments, all knowledge, prophecy, faith—what kind of faith?—so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing. He did not say: those things are nothing, but: if I do not have love, I am nothing. For who in his right mind would say: the sacraments of God are nothing? Who in his right mind would say: prophecy is nothing, knowledge is nothing, faith is nothing? Those things are not nothing, but when those things are great, I who have great things, if I do not have love, am nothing. Those things are great, and I have great things, and I am nothing if I do not have love, through which the great things I have benefit me. For if I do not have love, those things can be in me, but they cannot benefit me.
